startup.name: Polymath
startup.one_liner: Simulation environments for training & evaluating autonomous agents
startup.description: Polymath is a six person San Francisco data lab that builds reinforcement learning environments for training and evaluating long horizon software agents, including environments aimed at recursive self improvement. Buyers are AI labs and agent developers who pay per environment or per dataset. Revenue is not stated in the description.

yc_acceptance.basis: In this test the company is assumed accepted to YC for Winter 2026. Prior is about 1 percent. Six people in a category with strong lab demand sits above average, but many nearly identical RL environment companies applied, so the estimate is about 3 percent.
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: YC would most plausibly pass because RL environment startups are numerous, revenue is concentrated in a few lab buyers, and the pitch gives no named customer or contract. Partners would worry that a handful of data vendors already hold most of the budget.

outcomes.why_it_fails: The company fails to reach a meaningful exit if frontier labs insource environments, if demand shifts to a different training method, or if three or four large data vendors take most of the budget; similar RL environment companies have no recorded round beyond seed in the YC data.

analogs.relevance: Builds reinforcement learning environments, very close.
Frontier coding data for training and evaluating models.
RL environments and training data for labs.

killers.risk: Buyer concentration: few labs hold the budget
killers.evidence: Reports say most training data revenue sits with four large vendors and about a dozen buyers.
killers.mitigation: Sign multi-lab contracts and sell tooling as well as environments.

killers.risk: Frontier labs build environments in house
killers.evidence: Labs have the engineers and the incentive to own environments that define their models.
killers.mitigation: Specialize in long horizon work labs cannot staff.

killers.risk: Crowded field of near identical startups competes on price
killers.evidence: Many YC companies in 2025 and 2026 sell RL environments with the same pitch.
killers.mitigation: Focus on evaluation quality and verified difficulty.

competition_now.name: Scale AI, Surge AI, Mercor
competition_now.what: Large data vendors adding RL environments

technical_complexity.rationale: Environments require realistic software tasks and reliable graders, which a six person team can build, but long horizon difficulty and avoiding reward hacking are hard. Moat comes from quality, not a technical barrier.

takeover_risk.rationale: Large data vendors already sell environments and can copy offerings in months. Labs can also build their own, so the product is easy to absorb.

evidence.claim: Silicon Valley investors and labs are spending on environments to train agents.
The category has dozens of vendors, with revenue concentrated in a few.

actions: Pitch five labs with a working environment

pros.evidence: Labs are actively buying environments to improve agents.

pros.point: Team of six is above the typical YC size
pros.evidence: Suggests more build capacity than the usual two founders.

brand.name: Polymath
brand.name_check: python3 -I scripts/name_features.py --score "Polymath" --era 2022+ : 8 characters, 3 syllables, real word
brand.weaknesses: Generic, many companies share the name, hard to own search
brand.rationale: A real word that suggests breadth is easy to remember, but it is generic and shared, which weakens search. Lab buyers choose on results, so the name has little effect.

narrative.headline: Hot category with real demand but concentrated buyers and many copycats, so a seed is likely and later rounds are uncertain.
narrative.general_summary: Polymath sells reinforcement learning environments to AI labs, a category with real spending and a surge of YC entrants. Demand is real, but revenue is concentrated in a few large vendors and a dozen buyers, and frontier labs can build their own. A seed above the YC check is somewhat more likely than the cohort average because the sector is hot and the team is six people. Later rounds depend on recurring multi lab contracts, and the main upside path is a pivot from custom environments to a reusable platform or evaluation product. Reaching a round years later is common for companies with paying customers.

assumptions: Test is blind: only the YC input file was used for company facts.
Seed means a round above $500K within about 12 months.
Market figures from secondary blogs are unverified.
